sounds.name: Super Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of late-1990s trance supersaw pads
sounds.blurb: A wide, shimmering wall of detuned sawtooths that swells in and hangs.
sounds.how: DDS 1’s super mode spreads its sister oscillators either side of the centre one, so one sawtooth becomes a thick, beating stack. A slow attack and release make it a pad, a darker filter keeps it smooth, and both choruses together widen it into an ensemble.

steps.title: One sawtooth becomes a stack
steps.why:
DDS 1 holds seven oscillators; SUPER brings in the sisters and PW/DETUNE spreads them.
- UPPER SUPER ON: the sisters join the centre oscillator.
- UPPER PW/DETUNE 60 %: spread far enough to beat and shimmer.
- Listen for: one plain sawtooth turning into a wide, moving chorus of them.

steps.title: Fade it in and out
steps.why:
Envelope 2 shapes the loudness.
- UPPER ENV 2 A 1.0 s: each chord swells in.
- UPPER ENV 2 R 1.6 s: a long tail, so the chords overlap.
- Listen for: soft beginnings and long, melting endings.

steps.title: Darken it
steps.why:
A lower cutoff takes the fizz off the stack.
- UPPER LPF 1.8 kHz: warm rather than bright.
- UPPER RES 20 %: a slight edge at the cutoff.
- Listen for: the same pad, smoother and less buzzy.

steps.title: Widen it
steps.why:
Both chorus buttons together give the dense ensemble.
- CHORUS I on: the subtle chorus.
- CHORUS II on: with II as well, the string-machine ensemble.
- Listen for: the pad spreading out across the speakers.

context.up.pwDetune: How wide and thick the super stack is.
context.up.e2a: How slowly each chord fades in.

tweaks.hear: Just the centre sawtooth: how much of the sound is the stack.

sounds.name: Strings over Brass
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s film-score layered synth orchestras
sounds.blurb: A slow string pad and a punchy brass on every key, played together.
sounds.how: KEYBOARD on DUAL plays both layers on every key. The upper layer is a slow super-saw string pad; the lower is a brass, its filter swept open and shut by envelope 1 for the blare at the start of each chord. DETUNE puts the lower layer a fraction sharp, so the two beat together.

steps.title: Two layers on every key
steps.why:
DUAL stacks the upper and lower layers.
- KEYBOARD DUAL: both rows of controls play on every key.
- DETUNE +0.1 st: the lower layer a shade sharp, so the layers beat slowly.
- Listen for: one sawtooth getting thicker as the second layer joins it.

steps.title: The upper layer: strings
steps.why:
The top row becomes a slow, wide string pad.
- UPPER SUPER ON: a thick sawtooth stack.
- UPPER PW/DETUNE 50 %: a gentle spread.
- UPPER ENV 2 A 630 ms: the strings fade in.
- UPPER ENV 2 R 1.0 s: and fade away slowly.
- UPPER LPF 1.8 kHz: soft and warm.
- Listen for: a slow string swell under everything.

steps.title: The lower layer: brass
steps.why:
The bottom row is a brass: envelope 1 sweeps its filter open and back.
- LOWER LPF 448 Hz: dark at rest.
- LOWER VCF ENV 55 %: each chord opens it up.
- LOWER ENV 1 A 63 ms: the sweep takes a moment, the brass “blare”.
- LOWER ENV 1 D 250 ms: then settles.
- LOWER ENV 1 S 30 %: to a mellow sustain.
- Listen for: a bright, brassy push at the start of each chord, under the strings.

steps.title: Balance and widen
steps.why:
Set the layers’ levels and spread the whole thing.
- LOWER VCA ENV LEVEL 70 %: the brass a little under the strings.
- CHORUS I on: a gentle chorus over both.
- Listen for: a full, blended orchestra.

context.lo.vcaEnv: The balance of brass against strings.

tweaks.hear: The strings alone: what the brass was adding.
The brass a fifth above: a big, open interval.

sounds.name: Split Bass and Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-pop played by one keyboardist
sounds.blurb: A round bass under the left hand and a bright, gliding lead under the right.
sounds.how: KEYBOARD on SPLIT gives the keys below C4 to the lower layer and the rest to the upper. The lower layer is a short square bass with its sub-oscillator; the upper a sawtooth lead with DDS 2 a fifth up and a touch of portamento. Each hand plays its own instrument.

steps.title: One keyboard, two instruments
steps.why:
SPLIT shares the keys out between the layers.
- KEYBOARD SPLIT: the lower layer below C4, the upper from C4 up.
- Listen for: the same sound either side of middle C, for now.

steps.title: The left hand: a bass
steps.why:
The lower layer becomes a short square bass with a sub-oscillator.
- LOWER DDS 1 WAVEFORM square: hollow and round.
- LOWER DDS 2 RANGE LFO: DDS 2 leaves the sound…
- LOWER SUB OSC square (middle): …and the middle position brings in the square sub-oscillator.
- LOWER MIX 60 : 40: the sub well up under DDS 1.
- LOWER LPF 448 Hz: dark and round.
- LOWER VCF ENV 30 %: a soft pluck on each note.
- LOWER ENV 1 D 40 ms: a quick pluck.
- LOWER ENV 1 S 0 %: that closes fully.
- LOWER ENV 2 R 10 ms: the notes stop cleanly.
- Listen for: a deep, tight bass in the left hand.

steps.title: The right hand: a lead
steps.why:
The upper layer becomes a bright lead, DDS 2 a fifth above DDS 1.
- UPPER DDS 2 TUNE +7 st: a fifth up.
- UPPER MIX 60 : 40: both oscillators heard.
- UPPER RES 30 %: a little bite.
- Listen for: a big, open lead above middle C.

steps.title: Let the lead glide
steps.why:
PORTAMENTO on the upper layer only, so the bass stays tight.
- PORTAMENTO layer UPPER: portamento goes to the upper layer.
- PORTAMENTO 270 ms: a short slide between lead notes.
- Listen for: the lead sliding between notes while the bass stays put.

context.lo.mix: How much sub-oscillator weight is in the bass.
context.perf.porta: How far the lead slides between notes.

tweaks.hear: Both sounds on every key: a thick, odd hybrid.
The sine sub instead: a softer, rounder low end.

sounds.name: Sync Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Daft Punk — “Robot Rock”
sounds.blurb: A tearing, vocal hard-sync lead that snarls at the start of every note.
sounds.how: SYNC restarts DDS 2 with every cycle of DDS 1, so DDS 2’s pitch changes its tone rather than its note. Envelope 1 sweeps DDS 2’s pitch down on each key through the DDS modulator, which is the classic sync “tear”. SOLO and a little portamento make it a lead.

steps.title: Sync DDS 2 to DDS 1
steps.why:
Hard sync, with DDS 2 tuned up and heard on its own.
- UPPER DDS 2 MODE SYNC: DDS 2 restarts with each cycle of DDS 1.
- UPPER DDS 2 TUNE +5 st: tuned up, so its waves are cut off mid-cycle.
- UPPER MIX 0 : 100: only DDS 2.
- Listen for: a hard, nasal edge instead of a plain sawtooth.

steps.title: Sweep the sync
steps.why:
Envelope 1 moves DDS 2’s pitch on every key: the tear.
- UPPER DDS MOD destination DDS 2: the modulator acts on DDS 2.
- UPPER DDS MOD ENV 1 60 %: a big sweep.
- UPPER ENV 1 D 160 ms: over a fifth of a second or so.
- UPPER ENV 1 S 0 %: and right down.
- Listen for: each note snarling and settling.

steps.title: Make it a lead
steps.why:
One note at a time, sliding.
- VOICE ASSIGN MODE SOLO: one note at a time.
- PORTAMENTO 160 ms: a quick slide.
- UPPER RES 30 %: a little more bite.
- Listen for: a single, gliding, snarling lead.

tweaks.hear: No sync: a pitch swoop instead of a tone sweep.
With SYNC, CROSS MOD runs backwards and roughens DDS 2’s wave.

sounds.name: Sub Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of 2010s synthwave basslines
sounds.blurb: A deep, warm bass with a sine sub-oscillator underneath.
sounds.how: Turning DDS 2’s RANGE to LFO frees its place in the mixer for the sub-oscillator; the switch at the top picks the sine sub, an octave below DDS 1. A square DDS 1, a dark filter and a short envelope pluck finish it.

steps.title: A sine an octave below
steps.why:
DDS 2 at LFO range makes room for the sub-oscillator.
- UPPER DDS 1 WAVEFORM square: a hollow square on top.
- UPPER DDS 2 RANGE LFO: DDS 2 leaves the sound.
- UPPER SUB OSC sine (top): the top position picks the sine sub.
- UPPER MIX 50 : 50: equal parts square and sub.
- Listen for: a deep, solid low end under the square.

steps.title: Darken and pluck
steps.why:
A dark filter and a short envelope keep it round with a soft attack.
- UPPER LPF 317 Hz: round, not buzzy.
- UPPER VCF ENV 35 %: a little flick open on each note.
- UPPER ENV 1 D 40 ms: quickly.
- UPPER ENV 1 S 0 %: closing again.
- Listen for: a soft “dum” on every note.

steps.title: Tighten it
steps.why:
Short releases keep a fast bassline clean.
- UPPER ENV 2 S 70 %: a slight dip after the start.
- UPPER ENV 2 R 10 ms: notes stop cleanly.
- Listen for: tight, even notes.

context.up.mix: How much of the weight is the sub.

tweaks.hear: The square sub: a buzzier, more present bottom.
The filter overdriven: thicker and grittier.
No sub: how much weight it was adding.

sounds.name: Ring Mod Bells
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s electronic bell and gong sounds
sounds.blurb: Clangorous, inharmonic bells that ring and die away.
sounds.how: RING multiplies DDS 1 by DDS 2, leaving their sum and difference pitches instead of either note: with DDS 2 tuned to an odd interval the result is metallic, like a bell. A fast attack and a long decay with no sustain make each key a strike.

steps.title: Ring modulate the oscillators
steps.why:
RING puts DDS 1 × DDS 2 in DDS 2’s place; MIX brings it in.
- UPPER DDS 1 WAVEFORM sine: a pure tone.
- UPPER DDS 2 WAVEFORM sine: another.
- UPPER DDS 2 MODE RING: their product, not their sum.
- UPPER DDS 2 RANGE 4′: DDS 2 an octave up…
- UPPER DDS 2 TUNE +3.7 st: …and an odd interval more.
- UPPER MIX 10 : 90: mostly the ring modulator.
- Listen for: a clangy, bell-like tone that is no clear note.

steps.title: Strike and ring
steps.why:
No sustain and a long decay: each key is a strike.
- UPPER ENV 2 D 1.6 s: a long ring.
- UPPER ENV 2 S 0 %: dying away even while held.
- UPPER ENV 2 R 1.0 s: and still ringing after the key.
- UPPER LPF 10 kHz: open, so the clang is heard.
- Listen for: bells that ring on and fade.

steps.title: A room for them
steps.why:
Some delay gives the bells space.
- UPPER DELAY SEND 40 %: a little of the layer to the delay.
- DELAY TIME 440 ms: well-spaced echoes.
- Listen for: the bells answering themselves.

context.up.mix: How much of the sound is the ring modulator.

tweaks.hear: A whole-number ratio: a hollow, nearly musical tone.
A harsh, crowded clang from all the harmonics.
The plain sine coming back under the clang.

sounds.name: Cross-Mod Keys
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s digital electric pianos
sounds.blurb: A glassy, bell-tinged electric-piano tone that mellows as it rings.
sounds.how: CROSS MOD lets DDS 2 frequency-modulate DDS 1. With both on sines and DDS 2 two octaves up, a little FM gives the glassy “tine” of a digital piano. Envelope 1 sweeps DDS 2’s pitch so the attack is brighter, and DYNAMICS makes harder keys louder and brighter.

steps.title: FM from DDS 2 into DDS 1
steps.why:
CROSS MOD frequency-modulates DDS 1 with DDS 2, whose level stays out of the mix.
- UPPER DDS 1 WAVEFORM sine: a pure carrier.
- UPPER DDS 2 WAVEFORM sine: a pure modulator.
- UPPER DDS 2 RANGE 2′: two octaves up.
- UPPER CROSS MOD 35 %: a touch of FM: glassy, not harsh.
- Listen for: a bright, bell-like sheen on a sine.

steps.title: A piano’s decay
steps.why:
No sustain and a medium decay, like a struck note.
- UPPER ENV 2 D 1.6 s: a long fade.
- UPPER ENV 2 S 0 %: to silence.
- UPPER ENV 2 R 250 ms: a short ring after the key.
- Listen for: each chord fading like an electric piano.

steps.title: Play it with feeling
steps.why:
DYNAMICS makes harder keys louder and brighter.
- UPPER DYNAMICS ON: full velocity response.
- CHORUS I on: a gentle chorus.
- Listen for: soft chords mellow, hard ones ringing out.

context.up.xmod: How glassy or clangy the tone is.
context.up.dyn: How much playing harder changes the sound.

tweaks.hear: The modulator at unison: a growlier, reedy tone.
Every chord the same, however hard it is played.

sounds.name: Looping Envelope Pulse
sounds.ref: In the style of 2010s ambient-electronic pulses
sounds.blurb: Held chords that pulse and flutter by themselves, each note in its own time.
sounds.how: ENV 1 in LOOP repeats its attack and decay for as long as the key is held: an LFO that starts with each note. Sent to the filter it makes every held chord pulse. Envelope 1’s KEYTRACK shortens the loop on higher notes, so the notes of a chord drift out of step.

steps.title: Loop envelope 1
steps.why:
LOOP repeats attack and decay while the key is held.
- UPPER ENV 1 MODE LOOP: envelope 1 repeats.
- UPPER ENV 1 A 100 ms: a quick rise…
- UPPER ENV 1 D 250 ms: …and fall, about three times a second.
- UPPER ENV 1 S 0 %: down to nothing each time.
- Listen for: nothing yet: the loop is not routed anywhere.

steps.title: Pulse the filter
steps.why:
Send the looping envelope to a dark, resonant filter.
- UPPER LPF 224 Hz: dark between pulses.
- UPPER RES 50 %: a squelchy peak.
- UPPER VCF ENV 60 %: each pulse opens it.
- Listen for: every held chord pulsing on its own.

steps.title: Out of step
steps.why:
KEYTRACK shortens the loop on higher notes.
- UPPER ENV 1 KEYTRACK ON: each note pulses at its own speed.
- UPPER DELAY SEND 40 %: some delay to blur it.
- DELAY FEEDBACK 60 %: a long trail.
- Listen for: the notes of a chord fluttering against each other.

tweaks.hear: One sweep per key, then held: the loop is gone.

sounds.name: Arpeggio Echoes
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-pop arpeggios
sounds.blurb: A bright, plucked arpeggio climbing two octaves, its echoes filling the gaps.
sounds.how: The arpeggiator plays the held chord one note at a time at the TEMPO and CLK DIV, here eighth notes over two octaves. A short, plucky filter envelope makes each step pop, and the delay, timed against the tempo by ear, fills in between.

steps.title: Start the arpeggiator
steps.why:
Held chords play one note at a time.
- ARP on: the arpeggiator runs.
- CLK DIV 1/8: a step every eighth note.
- ARP RANGE 2: over two octaves.
- ARP MODE U&D: up and back down.
- Listen for: the chord turning into a running pattern.

steps.title: Make each step pluck
steps.why:
A short filter envelope pops each note.
- UPPER LPF 893 Hz: fairly dark at rest.
- UPPER VCF ENV 50 %: popping open on each step.
- UPPER ENV 1 D 100 ms: briefly.
- UPPER ENV 1 S 0 %: closing between steps.
- UPPER ENV 2 D 250 ms: each note dips…
- UPPER ENV 2 S 50 %: …to half level.
- Listen for: a bright plucked pattern.

steps.title: Echo it
steps.why:
The delay fills the gaps between steps.
- UPPER DELAY SEND 50 %: half the layer to the delay.
- DELAY TIME 410 ms: echoes about a dotted eighth apart at this tempo.
- DELAY FEEDBACK 50 %: a few repeats.
- Listen for: the pattern doubled and tangled by its echoes.

context.up.send: How much of the arpeggio echoes.

tweaks.hear: The arpeggio keeps running after the keys are let go.

sounds.name: PWM Strings
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s string-synth ensembles
sounds.blurb: A soft, swirling string section from one pulse wave.
sounds.how: DDS 2’s pulse wave has its width swept by LFO 1 through PW/WAVE: pulse-width modulation, the classic swirling string movement. A slow attack and release, the high-pass taking off some bass, and both choruses finish the ensemble.

steps.title: A pulse instead of DDS 1
steps.why:
DDS 2’s pulse, alone in the mix.
- UPPER DDS 2 WAVEFORM pulse: a pulse wave.
- UPPER MIX 0 : 100: only DDS 2.
- UPPER PW/DETUNE 30 %: a little narrower than square.
- Listen for: a reedy, hollow tone.

steps.title: Sweep its width
steps.why:
LFO 1 swings the pulse width through PW/WAVE.
- UPPER PW/WAVE source LFO 1: LFO 1 moves PW/WAVE.
- UPPER PW/WAVE 60 %: a deep sweep.
- UPPER LFO 1 RATE 0.40 Hz: slowly.
- Listen for: the tone swirling and shimmering.

steps.title: Make it a section
steps.why:
Slow in, slow out, and lighter in the bass.
- UPPER ENV 2 A 630 ms: the strings bow in.
- UPPER ENV 2 R 1.0 s: and fade.
- UPPER HPF 120 Hz: some low end taken off.
- UPPER LPF 2.5 kHz: soft on top.
- CHORUS I on: the chorus…
- CHORUS II on: …as an ensemble.
- Listen for: a lush, moving string section.

tweaks.hear: A still pulse: the movement was all PWM.
